papers.title: Analysis of a recent human parvovirus B19 outbreak using a new genomic surveillance system.
papers.abstract: Human parvovirus B19 is the causative agent of various clinical diseases like erythema infectiosum, transient aplastic crisis, fetal hydrops, reactive arthritis, and rarely potentially fatal organ diseases. The worldwide seroprevalence of parvovirus B19 has been assessed to be about 40-60%. It has been shown that parvoviruses can also infect new host species, adapt, and co-evolve. A comprehensive genomic surveillance is essential to gain a better insight in the adaptation, evolution, and also epidemics of parvoviruses. In the scope of the large parvovirus B19 epidemic 2023/24 following the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, we developed a rapid and convenient system to analyze parvovirus B19 genomes directly from patient samples by next-generation sequencing. We utilized this system to study the part of the unusual outbreak in Southern Germany (Central Franconia), comprising the counties Nuremberg, Fuerth, and Erlangen. This detected a certain genetic diversity within the analyzed samples and identified shared mutations in comparison to reference sequences. Here, two phylogenetically distinct groups were observed, compatible with the co-circulation of at least two B19V lineages in the region and a putative new genotype of human parvovirus B19, possibly induced by immunosuppression was identified. We established a new, quick, and convenient surveillance system for human parvovirus B19 that enables the analysis of outbreaks and monitoring of viral genetic changes.

papers.title: Nationwide clinical-genomic epidemiology of listeriosis in Taiwan, 2018-2025: disease manifestations in relation to clonal background.
papers.abstract: Listeriosis is an uncommon but severe foodborne infection, yet nationwide data linking pathogen genomics with clinical manifestations remain limited. We analyzed 1,252 laboratory-confirmed symptomatic listeriosis cases reported through nationwide surveillance in Taiwan during 2018-2025, with whole-genome sequencing of the corresponding clinical Listeria monocytogenes isolate from every case. The average annual incidence was 6.68 cases per 1,000,000 person-years, and 30-day all-cause mortality was 11.4%. Incidence showed an age-dependent sex pattern, with higher incidence among females aged 15-44 years and a shift toward male predominance at older ages. The female excess at ages 15-44 years persisted after exclusion of documented maternal-neonatal cases (male-to-female incidence rate ratio, 0.57; 95% confidence interval, 0.36-0.89). Clonal complex 87 (CC87) was the predominant CC (35.9%), whereas CC1 and CC2 were associated with higher odds of central nervous system (CNS) infection. LIPI-4 occurred predominantly in CC87, and LIPI-4-positive isolates showed lower odds of CNS infection; however, this association could not be separated from clonal background. More broadly, most associations of pathogenicity islands, virulence genes, and their alleles with disease manifestations could not be separated from the underlying clonal backgrounds in which these markers occurred, and none of the estimable associations remained significant after CC adjustment. This nationwide clinical-genomic study characterizes the contemporary burden of listeriosis in Taiwan and highlights clonal background as essential context for interpreting associations between virulence markers and disease manifestations.

papers.title: Exploration of tumor genomics associated with prolonged benefit from or resistance to talazoparib monotherapy in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibition is synthetically lethal in cells with deleterious alterations in DNA damage response genes involved in homologous recombination repair (HRR). Alterations in HRR genes, including BRCA1/2, have been identified in ~25% of prostate cancer samples and linked with worse clinical outcomes. We explored relationships between tumor genetics and prolonged benefit with talazoparib in TALAPRO-1. The phase II TALAPRO-1 trial evaluated talazoparib monotherapy in pretreated patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with HRR gene alterations. Tumor genetics were retrospectively assessed in subgroups in the efficacy population (n = 104) based on radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS: ≥12 months; ≥2 to <12 months; <2 months). Serial circulating tumor DNA samples from weeks 1, 9, and 25 and the safety follow-up visit (SFUV) were assessed for emergent changes in mutational profiles using FoundationOne®Liquid CDx. Among 16 patients with rPFS ≥ 12 months, 15 (94%) exhibited tumor BRCA2 alterations vs. 6/27 (22%) patients with rPFS < 2 months (p < 0.00001). HRR gene reversions predicted to restore HRR gene function were detected in 7/27 patients (BRCA1 [n = 1], BRCA2 [n = 5], PALB2 [n = 1]) evaluable for emergent variants at week 25 and/or the SFUV. Emergent PARP1 variants predicted to truncate PARP1 and/or inhibit talazoparib binding were evident in 5/27 evaluable patients. Patients experiencing prolonged benefit typically exhibited tumor BRCA2 copy number loss. Reversion mutations of HRR genes and emergent PARP1 variants likely reflect selective pressure to escape talazoparib synthetic lethality and/or PARP trapping. NCT03148795.

papers.title: Molecular characteristics and clinical outcomes of ERBB2-activating mutation-positive non-small cell lung cancer: A Japanese nationwide real-world cohort.
papers.abstract: Erb-b2 receptor tyrosine kinase 2 (ERBB2)-activating mutations are well-documented oncogenic drivers in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), occurring in approximately 1-4% of cases. These alterations include a heterogeneous spectrum of variant subtypes; however, the clinicogenomic characteristics and clinical significance of the individual variants have yet to be elucidated. We searched the nationwide Center for Cancer Genomics and Advanced Therapeutics database, which integrates comprehensive genome profiling data generated in routine clinical practice across Japan, to investigate the molecular landscape and clinical outcomes of patients with ERBB2-mutated NSCLC. A total of 319 patients with ERBB2-activating mutations were included in this retrospective analysis. Although 74% of the patients harbored canonical tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) in-frame insertions, 26% carried noncanonical variants, including TKD missense (8%), transmembrane/juxtamembrane domain (10%), and extracellular domain (ECD) mutations (8%). Co-occurring oncogenic driver alterations were identified in only 18 cases (5.6%) and were largely restricted to noncanonical variants, whereas no co-occurring driver alterations were detected among patients with TKD in-frame mutations. Noncanonical variants-TKD missense and ECD mutations in particular-were associated with an increased tumor mutational burden. Among 288 patients with available survival data, 78 (27%) received trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) during their clinical course. After excluding patients who had started treatment with T-DXd before undergoing comprehensive genome profiling testing, time-dependent T-DXd exposure was associated with a reduced risk of death (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.63; 95% confidence interval, 0.39-1.01; P = 0.057). ERBB2-mutated NSCLC exhibited substantial molecular heterogeneity, with canonical TKD in-frame insertions characterized by a low frequency of co-occurring oncogenic driver alterations. Among patients harboring ERBB2-activating mutations, exposure to T-DXd was associated with improved overall survival.

papers.title: PMA-qPCR for viability and phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing of Acinetobacter baumannii to four mechanistically distinct antibiotics in bronchoalveolar lavage.
papers.abstract: Due to its resistance to broad-spectrum antibiotics, Acinetobacter baumannii has become a predominant nosocomial pathogen. Thus, precise detection of viable bacteria and antimicrobial resistance is urgently needed. A PMA-qPCR assay was developed for the rapid, direct detection of viable Acinetobacter baumannii and antimicrobial susceptibility determination from bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, with its performance validated against targeted next-generation sequencing and culture. The assay demonstrated a detection limit of 1200 CFU/mL. In 59 clinical bronchoalveolar lavage fluid specimens, PMA-qPCR achieved a sensitivity of 90.91% (95% CI: 72.19 to 97.47) and 95.45% (95% CI: 78.2 to 99.19), and a specificity of 97.3% (95% CI: 86.18 to 99.52) and 91.89% (95% CI: 78.7 to 97.2) within 80 minutes, respectively, compared with targeted next-generation sequencing. After 45 minutes of antibiotic incubation, susceptibility testing for multiple antimicrobial agents was completed within 125 minutes. The performance of antimicrobial susceptibility testing is reliant on the mechanistic profile of the antibiotic. The highest overall agreement was observed for polymyxin B [100% (95% CI: 83.89 to 100)], which acts by targeting the bacterial cell membrane. Amikacin and ciprofloxacin, which inhibit protein synthesis and DNA replication/transcription respectively, yielded an overall agreement of 90% (95% CI: 69.9 to 97.21). By contrast, meropenem, a cell wall-active antibiotic, achieved the lowest overall agreement at 85% (95% CI: 63.96 to 94.76). Collectively, our results validate that PMA-qPCR serves as a rapid and reliable assay for the detection of viable Acinetobacter baumannii and antimicrobial resistance, thereby facilitating precise clinical decision-making.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Denoising-Enhanced Dual-Site CRISPR Cascade Nanosphere Enables Amplification-Free Pathogen Detection.
papers.abstract: Foodborne pathogens pose a major threat to global public health, necessitating rapid, sensitive, and deployable detection methods. Despite their considerable promise, current CRISPR-based diagnostics remain constrained by mandatory preamplification steps and insufficient sensitivity, hindering point-of-care application. Here, we introduce a self-supervised denoising-enhanced dual-site CRISPR cascade nanosphere (SD-DCCN) biosensing platform for on-site detection. The SD-DCCN integrates a CRISPR cascade architecture that reactivates the dormant catalytic potential of Cas12a by employing a universal split crRNA motif with two full-length crRNAs to synergistically boost the trans-cleavage activity, coupled with a self-supervised denoising algorithm on a visualized nanosphere platform that converts the amplified signal into a high-contrast quantitative readout. Our strategy eliminates the need for preamplification and achieves detection of Salmonella Typhimurium with a limit of detection as low as 16 CFU/mL, representing a 62.5-fold improvement over conventional amplification-free CRISPR assays. In addition, by integrating smartphone-readable tube analysis with qPCR-comparable sensitivity, the portable SD-DCCN presents a practical approach for rapid and on-site food safety monitoring. Furthermore, we quantify viable bacteria in diverse real food samples and validate the detection results against qPCR benchmarks. This platform holds great promise for CRISPR diagnosis of foodborne diseases, especially in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Fragment End Motif Analysis of Microbial Cell-Free DNA Improves Detection of Pathogens over Noise from Contaminants and Commensals.
papers.abstract: Circulating plasma microbial DNA (mDNA) is a promising biomarker for sepsis, but its accuracy is hindered by the low abundance of pathogen DNA and the presence of contaminants and commensals. mDNA enrichment using a selection of short fragments and single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) library preparation can improve pathogen yield but also increases background noise. Since nucleotide representation at mDNA fragment ends is biased by enzymatic digestion in vivo, we hypothesized that analysis of 5' and 3' mDNA fragment end motifs in enriched ssDNA libraries could improve pathogen detection. We performed deep metagenomic sequencing of size-selected ssDNA libraries from 38 plasma samples, including 20 samples from 5 sepsis patients, 18 samples from 6 patients without infection, and 6 no-template controls. Across these samples, we compared observed-to-expected ratios for end motifs in mDNA fragments from candidate pathogens and contaminants. For each candidate pathogen, we evaluated the accuracy of combining end motifs with microbial abundance for detection of infection. mDNA fragments from infection-causing pathogens were biased in the nucleotide motifs at both fragment ends compared with contaminants, with the highest enrichment observed in the GG dinucleotide at the 3' end (P < 0.0001). Integrating microbial abundance with end motif features improved differentiation between clinically significant pathogens and corresponding noise from the same microbes in noninfection samples. For Staphylococcus infections, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for the combination model was higher than than that for microbial abundance alone (0.892 vs 0.431, respectively; P = 0.018). mDNA end motif analysis improves signal-to-noise ratio beyond microbial abundance alone and improves pathogen detection in plasma metagenomic sequencing.

papers.title: Lateral Flow Immunoassay Technology for Blood-Based Infection and Sepsis-Related Biomarker Detection: Trends, Analytical Performance, and Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: The assessment of infection and sepsis remains challenging because microbiological methods are time-consuming and host-response biomarkers are not sufficiently specific across clinical settings. With its turnaround time, low sample volume, portability and ability to use whole blood, serum and plasma, lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) provides a viable approach for decentralized measurement. This review examines LFIA platforms for procalcitonin, C-reactive protein, serum amyloid A, interleukin-6, pathogen antigens and multiplex panels. Special focus is placed on colorimetric, time-resolved fluorescence, quantum-dot, chemiluminescent, Raman, electrochemical, and smartphone-based readouts. The performance characteristics are evaluated with respect to analytical parameters, including detection and quantification limits, precision, calibration, and agreement with reference methods. The limitations due to hematocrit, viscosity, anticoagulants, hemolysis, and incomplete plasma separation are considered. There are platforms that demonstrate analytical sensitivity and show agreement with immunoassay platforms, but studies rely on spiked samples, single-centre cohorts, or nontransferable cutoff values. While multiplex formats may enhance biomarker discrimination, they do not resolve differences in concentration ranges or calibration complexity. Clinical translation is dependent on validation using native whole-blood samples, readouts, lot-to-lot quality control, decision thresholds, prospective studies in multiple centers and evidence that LFIA-based testing enhances antimicrobial stewardship and patient care across intensive-care settings.

papers.title: Transmission of Xanthomonas translucens Associated with Wheat and Barley Seed.
papers.abstract: Bacterial leaf streak (BLS), caused by Xanthomonas translucens pv. undulosa (Xtu) and X. translucens pv. translucens (Xtt) on wheat and barley, respectively, persists as a threat to wheat and barley production. Seed is often implicated as a source of primary inoculum, despite conflicting historical reports. To clarify the role of seed transmission and track pathogen movement, seed of BLS susceptible wheat ('Mayville') and barley ('Pinnacle') was inoculated with rifampicin-resistant Xtu and Xtt strains, respectively. Pathogen colonization was assessed in tissue culture box assays and across field trials (2022 to 2024). Under the controlled environmental conditions of the tissue culture boxes, transmission from inoculated seed into the coleoptile and primary leaf tissues was 100% for both hosts, although the recovery of bacteria was often not accompanied by visual water-soaked symptoms, indicating asymptomatic colonization. In field trials, generalized linear mixed models confirmed that seed inoculation significantly increased the probability of bacterial detection in plant tissue throughout the growing season. Although Xtu successfully colonized inoculated wheat plants during plant development, the rifampicin-resistant strain was not recovered from any of the mature wheat seed that was harvested. In contrast, the rifampicin-resistant Xtt strain was recovered from two-thirds (66.7%) of the barley seed samples harvested at maturity. These results confirm that seed-associated X. translucens can colonize and persist within both wheat and barley, but they highlight a fundamental difference in the long-term persistence and seed contamination rates between Xtu and Xtt. Our results have significant implications for host-specific management and seed certification programs for the control of BLS.

papers.title: Rare LRRFIP1 variants contribute to the pathophysiology of severe early-onset scoliosis and common scoliotic phenotypes.
papers.abstract: Despite enormous advances in clinical genomics, idiopathic scoliosis remains an enigmatic condition with poorly understood genetic and pathophysiological underpinnings impeding molecular diagnosis and the development of targeted treatments. We performed linkage analysis, exome, genome and short- and long-read RNA-seq in a multigenerational family affected by autosomal dominant early-onset scoliosis (EOS) with a unique pattern of spondylodysplastic elements and progressive endplate erosion and identified the LRR-binding FLII-interacting protein 1 (LRRFIP1) gene as the disease-causing gene. The underlying cause is a rare noncoding variant altering transcription factor binding of nuclear receptor subfamily 3 group C member 1 (NR3C1) (glucocorticoid receptor), leading to changes in LRRFIP1 isoform expression. Transcriptomic changes in fibroblasts of affected individuals indicated a combination of disturbed Wnt signaling during somitogenesis, planar cell polarity signaling, and postnatal inflammatory dysregulation with clinical and molecular overlaps with ankylosing spondylitis and Scheuermann's kyphosis. We conducted a rare variant enrichment analysis using genome data from 484,903 UK Biobank participants and found an enrichment of rare risk-increasing LRRFIP1 variants in individuals with scoliosis. Our analysis of an Lrrfip1tm1.1(KOMP)Wtsi-KO mouse model showed an increased prevalence of idiopathic kyphoscoliosis in Lrrfip1-deficient mice. Our work provides insights into the pathophysiology of rare and common spinal disorders and hints at potential future therapeutic approaches with selective NR3C1 inhibitors.

papers.title: Herpes Simplex Virus Type 1 Isolated From Newborns Reveals Viral Diversity Between and Within Patients.
papers.abstract: Herpes simplex virus (HSV) type 1 and 2 infect over 14 000 newborns each year globally, with most cases (55%) causing a severe outcome that can be fatal if untreated. Neonatal disease severity and long-term outcomes remain unpredictable, and elucidating viral factors that contribute to these outcomes remains a challenge. However, through viral genomic and phenotypic analysis of HSV isolated from neonatal patients, we can begin to connect aspects of viral diversity with clinical patient data. Here we have applied viral whole-genome sequencing to a collection of residual clinical diagnostic samples from 10 neonates who had either mild or severe HSV-1 infections. Samples from different body sites or across recurrences allowed for both within- and between-host comparisons. From 30 residual diagnostic samples, we successfully isolated 14 viral cultures. These cultured viruses enabled additional phenotypic analyses, including in vitro growth evaluation in multiple cell types and an in vivo murine model of infection. These data highlight the diversity found in HSV-1 isolated from neonates. Through comparative genomics approaches, we demonstrate both within- and between-host diversity of these samples. Growth of cultured isolates in cell-based assays and a murine model of infection reveal additional aspects of within- and between-host differences. Overall, this study presents the first investigation into the viral diversity of neonatal HSV-1, which is now more common in the United States than neonatal HSV-2. Through integration of phenotypic, genomic, and clinical data we characterized these neonatal viral samples to begin unraveling the complexity of neonatal HSV-1 infections.

papers.title: Advancements in understanding the pathogenic mechanisms of Treponema pallidum.
papers.abstract: Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum (T. pallidum) is the etiological agent of syphilis, which has been regarded as a great imitator with its multiple possible clinical manifestations. The mechanisms by which this spirochete enters the host, elicits inflammation, causes host cell damage, and persists in its natural host are not adequately understood. This review aims to briefly introduce the microbiology of T. pallidum as a unique pathogen and summarize the recent advancements in understanding the molecular basis behind the immune evasion mechanisms of this pathogen. The basic scientific discussions herein should provide a framework for understanding the clinical and epidemiological outcomes described in this review.

papers.title: Agri-food connectivity drives the resurgence and geographic expansion of human brucellosis in China.
papers.abstract: Agri-food systems are increasingly recognised as drivers of zoonotic disease emergence, yet the mechanisms by which modern food production, trade, and distribution reshape pathogen transmission remain poorly quantified. Here we integrate two decades of nationwide surveillance, epidemiological modelling, and phylogenomic analyses of 4215 Brucella genomes from 79 countries and regions to elucidate the drivers of brucellosis re-emergence in China. Nationwide, human cases increased by 282.6% between 2005 and 2023, far exceeding the 8.1% increase in sheep inventory. This decoupling indicates a fundamental shift in transmission pathways. In northern China, livestock reservoir and production indicators accounted for 88.9% of the relative model contribution, consistent with direct occupational exposure; whereas in southern China, the agri-food logistics and market connectivity domain showed the largest contribution (64.1%), providing quantitative evidence that modern food-distribution infrastructure now drives brucellosis risk in those regions. Demographic shifts reaffirm this transition, with marked incidence increases among children and the elderly, indicating expanded foodborne and household exposures. Phylogenomics reveals that China's epidemic reflects long-term endemic amplification of a dominant Brucella melitensis clade (Lineage 2.4), with a hierarchical hub-and-spoke transmission network linking northern pastoral source regions to historically non-endemic southern provinces through national livestock and logistics networks. Comparative genomics further identifies lineage-specific gene acquisitions, adaptive variation in the outer membrane protein Omp2b, and recurrent convergent disruption of puuD enriched among winter isolates. Together, these findings reframe brucellosis resurgence as an emergent property of agri-food connectivity and highlight domestic supply chains, transport hubs, and cold-chain infrastructure as priority targets for surveillance and intervent ion.

papers.title: Highly efficient RPA product degradation and expanded PAM recognition enable RPA-Cas3 detection of Clonorchis sinensis.
papers.abstract: Clonorchis sinensis is a major foodborne pathogen threatening aquatic food safety. Microscopy, the diagnostic standard, is laborious and often lacks sensitivity for low-intensity infections. Molecular strategies coupling isothermal amplification with CRISPR/Cas systems have attracted interest, but their reliability is often undermined by competition between amplification and detection and intrinsic limitations of Cas effectors, notably PAM dependence of Cas12a and nonspecific activation of Cas13a. To address these limitations, we used the type I-A CRISPR-Cas3 system (TsiCas3) from T. siculi. Because TsiCas3 displays trans-cleavage activity at 65 °C, a temperature that completely abolishes RPA polymerase activity, this temperature gap can be exploited to avoid interference. A one-tube, closed-reaction workflow was established where target DNA is first amplified by RPA at 37 °C for 20 min, then the temperature is raised to 65 °C. This shift simultaneously inactivates RPA polymerase and activates TsiCas3-Cascade, enabling specific amplicon recognition, trans-ssDNA cleavage, and fluorescence generation. The sequential temperature control physically separates amplification from detection, eliminates mutual interference, and requires no tube opening or reagent addition. Moreover, Cas3 efficiently and near-completely degrades the RPA amplicons, substantially reducing aerosol carryover risk. This closed-tube, contamination-resistant method provides a rapid, sensitive, field-deployable tool for C. sinensis detection and represents a practical addition to clonorchiasis control.

papers.title: Breaking the channel barrier: same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy enables seven-target respiratory virus detection on a six-channel PCR platform within 20 minutes.
papers.abstract: Respiratory pathogens with overlapping symptoms-including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, H5/H7/H10 avian influenza, and RSV-co-circulate and co-infect, demanding rapid multiplex screening at points of care. Conventional multiplex real-time PCR is constrained by hardware channel capacity (≤6), making it difficult to detect seven targets while distinguishing influenza A and B in a single tube. This work addresses the contradiction between high-order multiplexing and limited fluorescence channels without sacrificing speed or sensitivity. We developed a six-channel ultra-fast PCR platform detecting seven respiratory viruses in a single tube within 20 min, using a same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy. Influenza A and B share the FAM channel yet generate distinct melting peaks (∼12 °C difference, 84.8 °C vs. 72.3 °C), enabling accurate typing via melting curve analysis. Primers, probes, and enzymes are pre-embedded as lyophilized beads in sealed cartridges for fully automated sample-to-result operation. The assay achieved 100% detection at 5 copies/test for all targets, linearity (R 2 > 0.95) across 5-10 5 copies/test, 90-110% efficiencies, and no cross-reactivity against 39 non-target pathogens. Cartridges remained stable for 12 months at 25 °C. Validation on 271 clinical specimens showed 100% agreement with sequencing-verified single-plex qPCR. This work provides the first integration of melting-curve-based same-channel multiplexing with lyophilized cartridge technology on an ultra-fast PCR platform. By overcoming channel limitations while maintaining speed and sensitivity, the system offers a practical, field-deployable screening tool for decentralized respiratory pathogen detection in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Automated machine learning framework for interpreting paper-based biosensing of pathogens.
papers.abstract: Paper-based biosensors have emerged as a promising tool for the rapid detection of microbial contaminants. However, the interpretation of paper-based biosensor images commonly relies on manual intensity extraction and assay-specific decision criteria, while explicit thresholds for positive/negative classification are often not reported. Herein, an ML framework was developed for automated interpretation of paper-based colorimetric biosensor images across distinct paper-based biosensor studies targeting different pathogens. Using conventional normalized intensity, region-of-interest (ROI)-based descriptors, and image-only convolutional neural network approaches, within-study validation showed strong positive/negative classification performance. However, the optimized decision thresholds differed between studies, and this study-dependent shift resulted in degraded cross-study classification performance. We therefore introduced a color-space normalization approach that quantified each target signal according to its chromatic relationship with the paired positive and negative controls, rather than relying on single-channel fluorescence intensity alone. This color-space normalization improved the separation of positive and negative readouts across studies and yielded comparable decision-threshold ranges in both within-study and cross-study validation. Accordingly, the color-space normalization approach provided more stable cross-study classification than conventional single-channel normalization, ROI-based descriptors, and image-only deep learning approaches. The trained model and frozen decision threshold were applied to a separate dataset as a small proof-of-concept application. These results support ML-assisted biosensor interpretation as a means to automate image interpretation and establish more consistent decision boundaries for paper-based biosensor studies.

papers.title: Perfluorodecanoic acid (PFDA) exposure, through stabilizing HIF-1α to induce VEGF/VEGFR2 autocrine signaling, promotes colorectal cancer cell proliferation.
papers.abstract: Perfluorodecanoic acid (PFDA) is a persistent organic pollutant widely present in the environment and resistant todegradation. In recent years, due to its extensive use in industrial production and consumer products, PFDA continuously accumulates in organisms and has become a global public health concern. Although epidemiological data suggest a possible association between PFDA and various cancer risks, its specific carcinogenic mechanism, particularly in colorectal cancer development, remains unclear. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the effects of environmentally relevant concentrations of PFDA on the biological behavior of colorectal cancer cells and to elucidate. the underlying molecular mechanisms. In vitro, human colorectal cancer cell lines HCT116 and HT-29 were used as models. Our results demonstrated that PFDA treatment significantly enhanced the malignant phenotype of cancer cells in a dose-dependent manner. Colony formation ability was enhanced. Meanwhile, cell invasion capacity was also significantly improved. Additionally, PFDA exposure induced glycolytic metabolic reprogramming in cancer cells, a metabolic feature closely associated with rapid tumor growth and malignant progression. To further elucidate the mechanism, our team conducted in-depth molecular biological investigations. The study found that PFDA does not affect gene transcription but instead directly binds to and stabilizes the VHL protein, preventing its degradation of HIF-1α. This consequently significantly upregulates its classic downstream target genes, VEGF and its receptor VEGFR2, thereby activating key downstream pro-survival and proliferation signaling pathways. Using a nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft model, our data also confirmed that in vivo PFDA exposure promotes tumor growth, with significant increases in both tumor volume and weight. In summary, this study lays a solid foundation for further in-depth toxicological research on PFDA.

papers.title: Identifying GSTM1, SDC1, and VTN as key biomarkers and therapeutic targets for NETs in acute pancreatitis based on bioinformatics analysis and experiments.
papers.abstract: Acute pancreatitis(AP) is a severe inflammatory disease associated with high morbidity and mortality. Emerging evidence suggests that neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) play a pivotal role in AP pathogenesis; however, effective therapeutic targets and interventions remain poorly understood.We conducted weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) on two independent transcriptomic datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus to identify disease-associated gene modules. Differential expression analysis of NET-related genes was performed, followed by functional enrichment analysis and protein-protein interaction network construction to elucidate biological pathways. Core genes were identified using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, random forest, and support vector machine recursive feature elimination algorithms. Network pharmacology was employed to predict potential therapeutic drugs. Finally, experimental validation was conducted using a caerulein-induced AP mouse and cell model.The WGCNA analysis identified 2707 key genes. Subsequently, combining differential expression analysis with machine learning approaches, we identified three core genes: glutathione S-transferase mu 1 (GSTM1), syndecan-1 (SDC1), and vitronectin (VTN). These genes exhibited significant expression alterations in AP. Drug prediction and molecular docking analysis revealed that semaxanib demonstrated strong binding affinity to all three target proteins. Experimental validation in the AP model confirmed the bioinformatics predictions: GSTM1 and VTN were significantly downregulated, while SDC1 was markedly upregulated.We identified NETs-related genes GSTM1, SDC1, and VTN as novel biomarkers for AP. Furthermore, semaxanib may have potential associations with pathways related to GSTM1, SDC1 and VTN, thereby participating to some extent in the intervention of acute pancreatitis. These findings provide a foundation for precision medicine approaches in AP management.

papers.title: Biological Characterization of Citrus Viroid VII.
papers.abstract: Citrus viroid VII (CVd-VII) was discovered in asymptomatic lemon trees in New South Wales, Australia, in 2015, and has not been recorded in other countries to date. There is a paucity of information known about the biological characteristics of this citrus-infecting apscaviroid. In this study, we investigated the host range, modes of transmission, and interactions of CVd-VII with other viroids. CVd-VII was mechanically transmitted to a range of Citrus species and varieties, causing asymptomatic infections, but a variety of plant species from different botanical families were shown to be nonhosts. CVd-VII was detectable in the seed testa and embryo, but grow-out tests suggested that it is not seed transmissible. The viroid could be detected in different tissue types from infected lemon and citron plants, but at differing titers, which emphasizes the importance of sample tissue choice for pathogen detection. The effect of coinfection of CVd-VII with other citrus-infecting viroids was evaluated in a greenhouse trial. Symptoms were more severe in coinoculated plants, particularly when CVd-VII was coinoculated with citrus dwarfing viroid and citrus exocortis viroid. This study highlights the potential impact of the viroid and the need to minimize its spread to avoid detrimental effects on citrus tree health and orchard productivity.[Formula: see text] Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). This is an open access article distributed under the CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International license.

papers.title: Photoelectrochemical interface mediated by S-scheme charge transfer and p-n heterojunction: Ultrasensitive detection of the emerging contaminant ornidazole.
papers.abstract: Ornidazole (ONZ) is a widely used nitroimidazole-class antibiotic whose environmental persistence due to misuse intensifies antimicrobial resistance and accelerates pathogen evolution, posing serious risks to human health and ecological safety. To address this issue, we developed a novel photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensor for ultrasensitive ONZ detection based on a p-n heterojunction between pseudobrookite-type oxide MgTi 2 O 5 and the metal-organic framework (MOF) Cu-BTC. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations corroborate the favorable band structure of the heterojunction. The built-in electric field and S-scheme charge transfer at the interface enable efficient separation of photogenerated carriers, yielding an ultralow detection limit of 0.65 pM, a wide linear range from 1 pM - 10 nM (R 2 = 0.9992), and excellent anti-interference, selectivity, stability and reproducibility. The sensor achieved 98.43% - 103.62% recovery in real samples including commercial capsules, tablets, and environmental water, demonstrating high practical reliability. This work presents a cost-effective, portable, and high-performance platform for ONZ monitoring and offers new insights into advanced PEC sensor design for antibiotic pollution detection.

papers.title: Azole resistance in Aspergillus series Nigri and possible link with environmental selection route.
papers.abstract: Resistance to medical azoles has been well investigated in Aspergillus fumigatus, which is primarily driven by exposure to azole fungicides. Azole resistance selection in other Aspergillus species remains understudied. We investigated azole resistance selection in Aspergillus series Nigri. 165 clinical series Nigri isolates were collected from Dutch and Belgian hospitals and 77 environmental isolates were obtained from air and other environmental sources, including known hotspots for azole resistance selection. Isolates were screened for resistance to medical azoles and selected fungicides using the EUCAST microbroth dilution reference method. Epidemiological cut-off values were used to identify non-wildtype isolates. All isolates were subjected to whole-genome sequencing, and global sequence databases were used for population genomic analyses. Clinical information was collected for azole-resistant isolates. Aspergillus tubingensis was the dominant species lineage among the clinical isolates (120/165, 72·7%), whereas species of the A. niger lineage were more frequently identified in environmental samples (55/78, 70·5%). Overall A. tubingensis isolates showed higher minimum inhibitory concentrations than A. niger isolates; 27 clinical isolates (17·0%) showed a non-wildtype phenotype for medical azoles as well as 24 of 78 (30·8%) environmental isolates. Sequencing revealed a worldwide distribution of multiple clonal groups. Cross resistance between medical azoles and azole fungicides was observed in A. tubingensis lineage isolates, which were recovered from hotspots, air and patient samples. Pan-azole resistant A. tubingensis was recovered from five mould-active azole-naïve patients, including a patient with proven invasive aspergillosis. Our study shows azole resistance in A. tubingensis lineage isolates and evidence that supports environmental resistance selection. Population genomics indicate a risk of global migration of resistant clones in A. tubingensis. Next to confirmative studies regarding black aspergilli, mycobiome analysis of hotspots are needed to identify potential selection of intrinsic or acquired resistant fungal species that may cause infections.

papers.title: Host-specific distribution of antimicrobial resistance in non-clinical Salmonella: a one health analysis of 791,298 isolates.
papers.abstract: The environmental distribution of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is frequently attributed to diffuse agricultural and aquatic reservoirs. To evaluate source-associated differences in AMR carriage, pre-computed genomic metadata for 791,298 Salmonella enterica isolates from the NCBI Pathogen Detection database were analyzed. Multivariate logistic regression, adjusted for serovar, geographic location, and database submission year, stratified non-clinical isolates into specific ecological niches against a human clinical baseline. Historical resistance (tetracycline) and mobilized colistin resistance (mcr) demonstrated profound concentration in poultry and swine environments. Crucially, while Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase (ESBL) carriage was negatively associated with swine, bovine, and generalized aquatic environments, poultry isolates exhibited an over four-fold increased relative prevalence (Adjusted OR = 4.03). Conversely, general aquatic environments consistently demonstrated a negative association across all resistance classes. These findings indicate that environmental AMR carriage within this database is highly compartmentalized, highlighting direct livestock production interfaces as primary targets for genomic surveillance.

papers.title: Peripheral detection of viruses shapes brain immunity and behavior in zebrafish
papers.abstract: Olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs) are constantly exposed to pathogens, including viruses. However, serious brain infection via the olfactory route rarely occurs. When OSNs detect a virus, they coordinate local antiviral immune responses to stop virus progression to the brain. Despite effective immune control in the olfactory periphery, pathogen-triggered neuronal signals reach the CNS via the olfactory bulb (OB). We hypothesized that neuronal detection of a virus by OSNs initiates neuroimmune responses in the OB that prevent pathogen invasion. Using zebrafish (Danio rerio) as a model, we demonstrate viral-specific neuronal activation of OSNs projecting into the OB, indicating that OSNs are electrically activated by viruses. Further, behavioral changes are seen in both adult and larval zebrafish after viral exposure. By profiling the transcription of single cells in the OB after OSNs are exposed to virus, we found that both microglia and neurons enter a protective state. Microglia and macrophage populations in the OB respond within minutes of nasal viral delivery followed decreased expression of neuronal differentiation factors and enrichment of genes in the neuropeptide signaling pathway in neuronal clusters. Pituitary adenylate-cyclase-activating polypeptide (pacap), a known antimicrobial, was especially enriched in a neuronal cluster. We confirm that PACAP is antiviral in vitro and that PACAP expression increases in the OB 1 day post-viral treatment. Our work reveals how encounters with viruses in the olfactory periphery shape the vertebrate brain by inducing antimicrobial programs in neurons and by altering host behavior.

papers.title: Kymograph classifiers predict CMT2A disease-relevant mitochondrial motility phenotypes in iPSC motor neurons
papers.abstract: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A (CMT2A) is a genetic disease characterized by autosomal dominant MFN2 mutations and dysregulated mitochondrial trafficking. While there is currently no FDA-approved CMT2A therapy, the recent development of iPSC motor neuron model systems, high-throughput imaging platforms, and CRISPR-based gene editing technologies holds promise for screening new therapies at scale in vitro. A critical roadblock for therapeutic screening is the development of scalable and robust computational methods to assess the mitochondrial trafficking phenotypes, healthy or diseased, of each iPSC motor neuron sample. To address this gap, we developed a vision transformer (ViT) based classification framework that predicts disease phenotypes using kymographs, an image transformation that captures particle movement along a prespecified path, such as mitochondrial movement along axons. We show that our classification approach more accurately discriminates healthy MFN2 wild-type (WT) from diseased MFN2 R364W-mutant (R364W) iPSCs than alternative summary statistics, such as mitochondrial speed and fraction of stationary mitochondria that are directly extracted from kymographs. Furthermore, we show that our model maintains high accuracy when deployed on a biological replicate holdout dataset. An analysis of ViT patch embeddings of the kymographs shows that mitochondria with highly variable sizes and many intersection events most strongly associate with R364W diseased kymographs. The computational approach demonstrated in this paper has broad applicability for future high-throughput screens where organelle trafficking along axons plays a key role in disease pathogenesis.

papers.title: EcoToxFred: A knowledge-graph-grounded conversational agent for exploring ecotoxicological monitoring and hazard data
papers.abstract: Assessing chemical risks to aquatic ecosystems requires the joint interpretation of monitoring data, ecotoxicity data, and derived risk indicators, yet such integrated data are rarely accessible to users without database expertise. We present EcoToxFred, an open-source conversational agent that provides natural language access to a curated knowledge graph of chemical monitoring and hazard data for European surface waters. EcoToxFred couples a large language model (LLM) with a Neo4j graph database in a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architecture. An agent interprets user questions, selects tools, translates questions into graph queries, and returns answers as text, tables, or interactive maps, together with the executed query for reproducibility. We evaluated EcoToxFred with GPT-4.1 and GPT-5 on a benchmark of 25 questions, including six questions derived from an expert workshop, each posed three times. Answers were scored for tool selection, execution accuracy against human-written reference queries, and goal accuracy using the RAGAS evaluation framework with an independent LLM judge. With both models, EcoToxFred selected an appropriate tool in at least 92% of runs and reproduced the reference result in 74% of runs with a reference query, including all lookup questions. Goal accuracy was 52% with GPT-4.1 and 63% with GPT-5. Failures concentrated on multi-step analytical questions, incomplete presentation of long results, and mismatches between user and database vocabulary. EcoToxFred shows how knowledge-graph-grounded LLM agents can lower the barrier to ecotoxicological data exploration while keeping answers traceable to the underlying data, and its architecture is transferable to other ecological data infrastructures.

papers.title: DeepCDS: Ab initio coding sequence prediction in prokaryotic metagenomic short reads
papers.abstract: Accurate coding sequence prediction in short prokaryotic metagenomic sequences, such as Illumina reads, remains challenging due to sequence fragmentation, unknown sequence origins, and sequencing errors. Here we introduce DeepCDS, a deep learning-based ab initio coding sequence predictor trained on short prokaryotic sequences with and without simulated Illumina-like sequencing errors. DeepCDS integrates embeddings from the protein language model ESM-2 with nucleotide-level information to predict complete and partial coding sequences. Benchmarking on 215 phylogenetically diverse prokaryotic organisms demonstrates that DeepCDS consistently outperforms well-established and widely used methods in coding sequence detection across sequence lengths from 75 to 1,000 base pairs, including improved identification of both canonical and non-canonical start codons as well as stop codons, and greater robustness to different sequencing error profiles. DeepCDS also recovers more coding sequences from functionally uncharacterized genes and remains operational on sequences shorter than existing tools support. We additionally evaluate DeepCDS on a simulated metagenomic dataset from the Critical Assessment of Metagenome Interpretation initiative, where it likewise achieves the strongest performance among tested tools, and on a real human gut metagenome, where its predictions are more frequently supported by known proteins. These findings suggest that amino acid-level context, here provided by a protein language model, contributes complementary information for nucleotide-level coding sequence detection, especially at very short lengths. Ultimately, DeepCDS may help uncover the functional potential of the vast microbial diversity that remains genomically uncharacterized.

papers.title: OrthoSimulator: Empirically trained simulations for ground-truth benchmarking of orthology inference
papers.abstract: Orthology inference is foundational for comparative genomics, enabling the reconstruction of phylogenetic relationships and transfer of biological knowledge between species. Methods often infer different orthogroups and orthologous relationships, making robust benchmarking essential for evaluating their accuracy. Existing resources such as the Quest for Orthologs benchmark service and OrthoBench provide valuable benchmarks grounded in real biological data and expert curation. However, the true evolutionary histories in all of these benchmarks are unknown, and therefore the true accuracy of orthology inference methods is unknown. Simulations provide an approach to evaluate accuracy where the complete ground truth is known. However, simulations are only useful for benchmarking if they realistically reflect empirical data. Here, we introduce OrthoSimulator, a Python package for generating realistic, empirically calibrated benchmark datasets with known orthogroups, orthologous relationships, gene trees, and evolutionary events. We demonstrate its utility by benchmarking widely used orthology inference methods across simulations calibrated from multiple methods and empirical datasets. We show that method-to-method variability in ortholog inference accuracy is robust to variation in simulation parameters. We further provide a detailed evaluation of ortholog inference accuracy through independent cross-validation, and show that OrthoFinder is the most accurate of the four methods tested. OrthoSimulator is freely available at https://github.com/lauriebelch/OrthoSimulator.

papers.title: Somatic mutation probabilities learned from the DNA sequence
papers.abstract: Somatic mutations distribute heterogeneously over genomes, dependent on immediate sequence context, function, and non-genetic factors. Mutations present the foundation for somatic genome evolution towards age-related diseases. Here, we present EAGLE-MUT, a group of DNA language models trained on sparse single base substitution data from esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) and melanoma (MELA) samples. In both cancer types, predicted mutation probabilities vary across several orders of magnitude, depending on sequence context. For example, T>G hotspots in EAC localize to A/T-rich ~200 base pair DNA motifs, associated with nucleosome positioning. Coldspots localize to G/C-rich DNA, nucleosome linker DNA, CTCF binding sites, potential origins of replication, and intron-exon boundaries with a transcription strand bias. Fine-tuning EAGLE-MUT for individual patient samples leads to varying mutation distributions relative to genome elements and potential cancer driver mutations. EAGLE-MUT provides new links between DNA sequence, genome function, and stability in individual samples, a foundation for understanding somatic genome evolution, and more personalized strategies for risk-assessment, prevention, and treatment.

papers.title: Know Thy Neighbour: Benchmarking Protein Language Model Embedding-Based Annotation Reveals Anisotropy Substantially Impacts Retrieval
papers.abstract: Functional annotation using protein language models (`pLMs') usually proceeds by transferring the function of a query's nearest neighbour in a reference database. A major drawback is that embedding-based annotation transfer has no null model, i.e. no accepted way to set a cosine-similarity threshold to control false positives. This contrasts with traditional bioinformatics methods, including sequence- and structure-based alignment tools, which rank hits with E-values derived from explicit null models. Here, we benchmark final-layer, mean-pooled embeddings from twelve models against MMseqs2 and Foldseek for remote-homology retrieval on curated datasets based on Swiss-Prot and SCOPe, fixing per-model thresholds at a 1% false-positive rate and probing the score with a ladder of synthetic decoys. On Swiss-Prot, pLMs without retrieval training recover at most 15% of remote homologs at this operating point, against 85% for MMseqs2, and for the ESM-2 and ESM-C families shuffled decoys have higher cosine similarities to their nearest database hits than real remote homologs do. These two pLM families exhibit extreme anisotropy, using fewer than 15 effective dimensions out of 640-2560, and low effective dimensionality is strongly associated with poor performance across models. Applying ZCA whitening, fit on the reference database, to the embeddings sharply raises threshold-free Top-1 superfamily retrieval, e.g. for ESM-2 650M from 59% to 88% on SCOPe, and generally improves remote homology sensitivity at a fixed false-positive rate. As correcting embedding anisotropy requires only the reference database and is compute cheap, it should be considered and tested for any pLM embedding-based annotation task.

papers.title: Evaluating Language Models as Orchestrators in a Tool-First Biomedical Discovery Platform
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly orchestrate agentic biomedical discovery systems, but cloud deployment raises concerns about inference cost, data privacy, and governance. Small language models (SLMs) that run on-premises are an alternative, provided they orchestrate scientific tools about as well as larger models. We built a tool-first, multi-agent system for scientific discovery in which an orchestrator coordinates six specialized tool systems: differential expression, literature retrieval, pathway enrichment, network-based gene prioritization and knowledge-graph analysis, perturbation signature matching, and structural/druggability assessment. In a tool-first design, specialized tools supply the domain knowledge and computation, so the model's main task is coordination, e.g. choosing tools, passing the right parameters, calling them in the right order, and carrying results across turns. With the tools, prompts, workflow, and benchmark held constant, we compared three orchestrators, Gemma 4 (26B, open-weight and locally deployable), Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 5. Evaluation used a custom benchmark of 104 single-turn and multi-turn tests, an LLM-as-judge protocol (groundedness and evidence validity), tool-use accuracy and efficiency metrics, and blind expert review. On single-turn tasks, the three models performed comparably, and reviewers did not rate the SLM below the larger models. In multi-turn tasks, Claude Sonnet 5 showed marginally higher evidence validity, Gemma 4 was weakest when parameters had to be assembled across turns, and all three models struggled with tool ordering on memory-dependent tasks. These differences were illustrated with case studies. Finally, we propose strategies to help SLMs address the multi-turn limitations and support cost- and privacy-aware deployment.

papers.title: ProtCOVER: Family-Aware Conformal Prediction for Variant Effect Predictors on Unseen Protein Families
papers.abstract: Protein language models and related variant effect predictors (VEPs) increasingly classify missense variants in proteins evolutionarily distant from those used for calibration. Split conformal prediction over variants is valid for its own target, a random variant dominated by well-studied families, but deployment needs coverage for a variant of a new family. On ProteinGym clinical substitutions with five zero-shot predictors, Mondrian conformal comes within 0.005 of that target for four predictors, yet family-weighted pathogenic coverage is only 0.823-0.873 at a 0.90 target for all five, without any shift. We present ProtCOVER, a conformal procedure that treats homology families, rather than individual variants, as the exchangeable unit. ProtCOVER (i) calibrates at the family level over label-free homology clusters, giving marginal coverage for a new family under family exchangeability; (ii) adapts to descriptor shift by calibrating conditionally on an estimated density ratio of label-free descriptors (sequence similarity, alignment depth and embedding distance; a variant reweights by the ratio instead), with finite-sample family-weighted coverage, valid as computed, whenever the true ratio is a nonnegative affine function of the estimate; and (iii) can abstain at low effective calibration support, which proved no better than random abstention. Under a shift of its descriptors, ProtCOVER's mean worse-class shortfall below the target is 0.000, against 0.010 for group-weighted and 0.029 for hierarchical conformal prediction, with larger sets (about equal at matched coverage); on orphan families and held-out embedding regions it matches group weighting (0.002 against 0.003). In evaluations following pre-registered protocols, every shift-aware method met the target on new ClinVar variants of benchmark proteins, which ESM-1b separated better; on 12,225 proteins outside the benchmark, every method fell short for pathogenic variants with either of two predictors, ProtCOVER and a variant conditioned on the descriptors the least, within the 0.01 margin of group weighting.

papers.title: From species-wide genomics to cellular diversity: characterizing multidrug-resistant extraintestinal pathogenic Escherichia coli ST744
papers.abstract: The species Escherichia coli represents a wide and heterogeneous range of strains. Here, we exploited this genomic diversity to examine the distribution of virulence-associated genes (VAGs) and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) within a collection of 131,610 E. coli genomes. Across lineages of extraintestinal pathogenic E. coli (ExPEC), we identified a negative correlation between VAG and ARG content, with ST744 carrying the most resistance genes on average. Phylogenomic analysis of a global ST744 cohort revealed the existence of two main clades, and substantial variation in accessory gene content, resistance-region organization, and plasmid carriage. Subsequent phenotypic characterization revealed that the interpretability of genomic information depends on the trait being considered. Whereas antibiotic susceptibility measurements generally agreed with genomic predictions, limited correspondence was observed between the presence of specific metabolic and stress-associated genes and enhanced growth under such conditions. Image-based profiling also revealed extensive diversity in cell morphology, nucleoid organization and cell-cycle timing across strains, even among nearly clonal isolates. Together, our findings provide an in-depth characterization of E. coli ST744, within the broader diversity of E. coli and EXPEC, as well as a framework for examining how genomic differences relate to phenotypic diversity within other ExPEC lineages.

papers.title: Systematic Benchmarking and Optimization of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for Clinical Phenotyping: A Type II Diabetes Case Study in an ICD-Screened Cohort
papers.abstract: Traditional EHR phenotyping methods can require substantial disease-specific development and long-term maintenance. While integrating large language models (LLMs) with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is promising, the impact of RAG configurations remains underexplored. We systematically evaluated these design choices for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) phenotyping in an ICD-screened cohort. Using GPT-4o, we processed 170,678 clinical notes from 275 patients. We evaluated seven embedding models and three prompt strategies (baseline, improved zero-shot, and few-shot). Using the improved zero-shot prompt, we tested 350 embedding model-chunk size-retrieval depth combinations on the training set and selected eight optimized configurations for test-set evaluation. Combined with three prompts, these yielded 24 prompt-configuration combinations for comparison with ICD codes and the institutional PheNorm method. RAG achieved a mean sensitivity of 0.9019 (95% CI: 0.8866-0.9172), specificity of 0.7907 (0.7749-0.8066), PPV of 0.9405 (0.9365-0.9445), NPV of 0.6967 (0.6653-0.7281), and F1-score of 0.9204 (0.9124-0.9283). All combinations achieved higher PPV than ICD codes (0.7838). Compared with PheNorm, sensitivity was significantly higher (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), while specificity differences were not significant. Paired bootstrap analyses showed higher NPV and F1-score , with no significant PPV difference. General-purpose embeddings showed higher sensitivity, whereas biomedical embeddings exhibited higher specificity and PPV. Few-shot prompting increased specificity and PPV but reduced sensitivity. Token usage varied substantially across embedding models. These findings suggest the importance of aligning RAG design with task-specific clinical priorities and token efficiency.

papers.title: Expert-level localization of fine-grained cardiac structures across the transthoracic echocardiogram
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence models for echocardiography interpret studies without identifying the structures that support their outputs. We show that this spatial grounding does not emerge from the pretraining of current vision-language models. General-purpose and medical vision-language models and an open-vocabulary detector recalled 3% or fewer of cardiac structures and scored below a box that never sees the image. EchoLens, a detector trained on 5,912 expert-annotated structures and 4,219 Doppler signals from 136 patients, recalled 87% and localized structures as reliably as a blinded expert reader (box centre within the reference in 95.7% and 95.3% of cases). It covers 21 structures across 11 transthoracic views and 11 spectral Doppler signal types. In external data, two physicians judged 81-92% of its detections correct across all 11 views, and it identified the Doppler signal type in 83% of frames. EchoLens provides the spatial layer that grounded echocardiographic interpretation requires.

papers.title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa in bronchiectasis: unmasking population diversity and antimicrobial resistance in the Australian context
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background: Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections in bronchiectasis airways result in poorer lung function, advanced lung lobe involvement, worsened life quality, and higher hospitalisation rates. Despite high prevalence, little is known about P. aeruginosa population genomics, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) rates, persistence, and transmission dynamics in Australians with bronchiectasis. Methods: P. aeruginosa (n=137) isolated between 2009 and 2025 from 59 Australians with bronchiectasis underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing against 11 antipseudomonal drugs, whole-genome sequencing, comparative genomics, and in silico AMR determinant identification. Data were integrated with 4,575 publicly available bronchiectasis-derived P. aeruginosa genomes to determine global phylogenomic and AMR determinant patterns. Results: High AMR rates were identified in the Australian isolates, with 75.9% resistant to at least one antimicrobial, 19.7% multidrug-resistant, and 9.5% extremely drug-resistant. AMR rates were highest (64.2%) for ciprofloxacin and cefepime (44.5%), and lowest for piperacillin/tazobactam (8.8%) and colistin (0.7%). Phylogenomics uncovered several instances of within-host evolution, hypermutation, persistence, and multi-lineage infections. Of the fifty-seven identified multilocus sequence types (STs), seven (12.3%) were novel, five were high-risk international clones (ST274 [6.6%], ST395 [0.7%], ST244 [0.7%], ST277 [0.7%], ST298 [0.7%]) and three were common global clones (ST253 [5.1%], ST155 [3.6%], ST260 [0.7%]). No high-risk AMR-conferring mobile genetic elements were seen, although numerous chromosomal AMR determinants were identified. AMR determinant prevalence was consistent with the global dataset, with no evidence of geographic clustering. Conclusions: Our study provides critical insights into P. aeruginosa diversity in Australians with bronchiectasis. High AMR rates and chronic colonisation highlight the need to improve diagnostics, antimicrobial stewardship measures, and infection control practices in this neglected clinical cohort.

papers.title: In-country cerebrospinal fluid metagenomic next generation sequencing for pathogen detection in Lima, Peru
papers.abstract: Background: Central nervous system (CNS) infections are a major cause of morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries such as Peru. However, their epidemiology is poorly characterized due to a wide range of endemic and opportunistic pathogens involved and limited access to specialized neurodiagnostic testing. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) can detect any pathogen in a single hypothesis-free assay but has largely been confined to reference laboratories in high-income countries due to high cost and infrastructure requirements. We piloted an in-country, research-based CSF mNGS protocol in Lima, Peru, as a proof-of-concept study to assess the feasibility of implementing this approach in a resource-limited setting. Methods: Adults admitted with suspected CNS infection at Hospital Nacional Dos de Mayo, a large public hospital in Lima, were enrolled from August 2024 to April 2025, and approximately 0.5-2 mL of surplus CSF was collected. CSF mNGS (DNA and RNA) was performed in-country on a benchtop sequencer with half-volume library reactions and cloud-based analysis (CZID). Paired sequencing at a significantly higher depth was performed on a subset of samples in the United States for validation. Results: Among 43 participants (median age 48 years; 21% living with HIV), mNGS performed in Peru detected 20 pathogens in 18 samples (42%), of which 65% were not identified by routine clinical testing. Nine of 15 patients treated empirically for tuberculous meningitis were found to have a non-mycobacterial infection. Detected organisms included Toxoplasma gondii, Taenia solium, Treponema pallidum, human T-lymphotropic virus 1, herpesviruses, and, on deeper sequencing, Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus. Deep sequencing yielded 3.7-fold (DNA) and 6.9-fold (RNA) more reads and recovered four pathogens missed at shallower-depth. Conclusions: In-country CSF mNGS was feasible in Lima, Peru and recovered a clinically and epidemiologically meaningful spectrum of CNS pathogens, most missed by routine testing. By utilizing available, lower-output sequencers, we overcame a principal barrier to deploying this technology where the burden of undiagnosed CNS infection is greatest.

papers.title: Wastewater metagenomic sequencing quantitatively tracks transmission dynamics for human pathogenic viruses
papers.abstract: Wastewater metagenomic sequencing theoretically characterizes all nucleic acids in a sample, but whether sequencing reads reflect transmission dynamics of circulating viruses in the contributing community is unknown. We evaluated if wastewater metagenomic sequencing data can be used to reconstruct transmission dynamics of endemic, routinely circulating viruses. Using deep, untargeted wastewater metagenomic sequencing data from four locations in the United States, we generated quantitative estimates of transmission dynamics (time-varying growth rate and effective reproduction number) within a Bayesian framework for widely monitored viruses. Across locations and viruses, estimates were statistically concordant with those derived from clinical surveillance and polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based wastewater monitoring data. Furthermore, we estimated growth rate from wastewater metagenomic sequencing data for numerous viruses not otherwise widely monitored, demonstrating the data expands the targets that can feasibly be monitored in parallel. Wastewater metagenomic sequencing can support both novel pathogen detection and routine surveillance of endemic pathogens.
